title: Alex Karp, Cold War Liberal
author: Geoff Shullenberger
content:
![Alex Karp, Cold War
Liberal](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/11/52099053970_d14073f75e.jpg)

In the wake of the midterm elections, memes and jokes abounded about Silicon
Valley grandees dying their hair blue and adding pronouns back to their email
signature lines to signal a strategic rapprochement with the victorious
Democratic Party. This week, Palantir CEO Alex Karp seemed to ratify these
expectations with an interview in which he declared himself and his company
"essentially progressive." It seemed to many like an abrupt, cynical _volte-
face_ for an executive who, perhaps more than anyone other than Elon Musk,
personified tech's rightward turn under the second Trump administration--and
benefited considerably from that reorientation.

But such analyses risk mistaking style for substance. Tech leaders' embrace of
right-wing aesthetics, exemplified by Mark Zuckerberg donning a "bro" uniform
for his 2025 appearance on _The Joe Rogan Experience_ , has too often obscured
the deeper transformations underway in the industry in recent years. Chief
among these is Silicon Valley's open embrace of the state. Karp's rhetorical
vacillations should not distract from the company's deeper consistency as an
early and aggressive champion of this alliance.

> deeper consistency."
